ratings_why.fun: The cooling triangle gives a curve I'd want to climb with: small early, a real choice mid-game between Quenching now and waiting, and quadratic late growth once the Furnace lands.
ratings_why.distinct: Decaying Heat, self-burns and the Quench cash-out are fresh, but at heart it is still 'stack buffs on one piece by position', which Hedgerow folk and many tribes already do.

verdict_why: The core works and each tier does its job; Ember-Slinger and the Reforge-stacking rule need clearer wording before more play.

points.text: Ember-Slinger says your units 'give' their Heat for this fight; say whether they get it back afterwards, or players can't tell if it costs them their Reforges.
Stacking 'Reforge twice' is unclear: does Crater Forge Master plus Thiers Grinder make 3 Reforges, and does golden 'three times' add two? Write the count rule into each card's reminder text.

Under the Undying Furnace, Heat climbs every turn and Yellowback Spitter's damage is uncapped, so late Start of Combat can wipe a front row. It's a great high roll; the owner may want a sim at turns 10 to 14.

Quench-Bucket Lad beats waiting at 1 to 3 Heat and loses to it above that, and loses badly under the Furnace. That's the tribe's best decision point; more Quench payoffs at Tier 4 would let the burst build climb too.
The last build entry's name is broken markup ('Mixing in a lobby.** - **Bog folk:'), so the lobby notes read as one garbled build.

standouts.why: A cheap, re-buyable Quench that makes 'cash out now or keep heating' a real choice from Tier 2.
One line turns the whole tribe's growth from a triangle into a climb, and it fights Warden Quench, so you must choose a lane.
Turns your own burn cost into an attack on the enemy across; a fresh Tier 5 direction card.

weakest.why: Gold for empty slots works against 'the board is the fight's HP' and barely touches Heat; likely a trap or a must-pick.
A generic sell trigger; the Ingot is fine but the card has nothing to do with position or reheating.
A quarter of lost Health rounds to little at mid-game stats, so the injury build's glue is slow until very late.

flags.note: Damage equals Heat with no cap; with the Undying Furnace it grows every turn and can clear boards before combat.
No cooling plus Konrad, Bellows and Paracel means Heat grows linearly and stats quadratically; golden heats every unit each turn too.
Up to four extra Reforges on the Hottest unit, multiplied by its Heat, stacks hard with the Furnace and Crater Forge Master.
Regrow giving Attack as well compounds up to x1.25 a fight on every unit, and burns guarantee the loss; needs the runaway check.
Whether your units keep or regain their Heat after the fight isn't stated.
How multiple 'Reforge N times' effects add up isn't on the card.
